source.text:
Hello,

Thank you for sending over the updated proposal last week.
Our leadership review has been moved from October 2 to October 9, because two of our directors will be traveling that week.
Could you send us the revised pricing sheet by September 30, so that we can include it in the pre-read?
We would also like to add a 15-minute demo of the reporting dashboard to the agenda.
Please let me know if that timing works on your side.

Best regards,

capture.label: Summarize
capture.instructions: Summarize the input to its essence in one short sentence, in {{ locale | language_name }}; output only the summary, no preamble.

turns.reply: The client has rescheduled their leadership review to October 9 and requested a revised pricing sheet by September 30, along with a 15-minute dashboard demo.

This message is a professional request to change the timing of a business meeting and update the materials needed for it. It matters because it ensures that the people in charge have the right information before they make a final decision.

Here is the breakdown of what the sender is asking for:

**A schedule change**
The people who need to look at the proposal are having their meeting one week later than planned. This is because two of the leaders will be away on a trip during the first week of October.

**A new document**
The sender wants an updated price list. They need this document by September 30. They use the term "pre-read" to describe this. A pre-read is simply a set of documents that people look at before a meeting starts so that everyone is already prepared when the discussion begins.

**Adding a demonstration**
The sender wants to add a short presentation to the meeting. They want to see a 15-minute demo of the "reporting dashboard." A dashboard, in this context, is a digital screen that shows important data and summaries in one place. A demo is just a live showing of how that tool works.

**Asking for agreement**
Finally, the sender asks if these new dates and the extra 15 minutes for the demo work for the person receiving the email. They are checking to make sure the other person is available and can get the work done in time.

This message is a request to adjust the timing of a business meeting and update the materials for it. It matters because it ensures the company leaders have the right information before they make a decision.

Here is what the sender is asking for:

**A new meeting date**
The meeting is moving from October 2 to October 9 because two leaders will be away.

**A document update**
The sender needs a revised price list by September 30. They want to include this in the "pre-read," which is the set of materials sent to people before a meeting so they can study the information ahead of time.

**A live demonstration**
The sender wants to add a 15-minute slot to the meeting to see a demonstration of the reporting dashboard. This is a digital screen where users can see summaries of their data.

**A confirmation**
The sender is asking if these new plans work for you and if you can finish the new price list by their deadline.
